protocol.weights: official current-wave weights normalized to equal total weight per month
protocol.inference: person-cluster CR1 with absorbed month count included in residual degrees of freedom
protocol.multiplicity: BH across the 16 primary factor/outcome joint Wald tests, separately within each period

prespecified_contrasts.education_fine: high school diploma code 2 minus bachelor code 5
prespecified_contrasts.financial_change: somewhat worse code 2 minus same code 3

protocol.sensitivity: Q8 capped at -100/+100, labelled sensitivity only; primary Q8 not trimmed
secondary: add seven individual quiz correctness variables beyond official high/low category, same complete cases
financial decision role among observed respondents, not imputed for structurally skipped cases
calendar-adjacent first differences for financial-change categories and Q8/Q9 outcomes
protocol.descriptive_distribution: monthly survey-weighted quantiles within groups, then equal-month averages; cross-person IQR and median individual density IQR reported separately
limits: Associations, not causal effects or learned behavioural weights.
Previously viewed data periods: temporal replication is not a new blinded experiment.
Current Q1 is subjective and can itself reflect inflation; reverse causality remains.
Stable entry traits cannot be identified in person fixed effects; first differences apply to changing Q1.
No current outcomes or fitted coefficients will be inserted into a simulation provider.
No causal identification: current Q1 and inflation beliefs may influence one another.
Month FE, observed controls and person clustering do not resolve every omitted variable or shared residual shock.
Risk, education and financial role are observed entry traits carried only forward; not experimentally assigned behaviour.
First differences cancel stable person effects but not time-varying confounders or survey measurement error.
Adjacent forecasts have rolling overlapping 12-month horizons; revisions are not fixed-target Bayesian updates.
Conditional regression coefficients refer to means; descriptive group medians/IQR are separate objects.
Descriptive distributions are not population-standardized for all controls. Secondary models are exploratory.
No simulation inputs changed, no observed current target values exported to a provider.
